# Pinned external structural conformance selection

These are unchanged files from W3C's XML Schema test suite, contributed by Microsoft, at revision `7bc3365c652a322f3d762021b3879eb92dae7e30`. Original copyright is retained at `upstream/00COPYRIGHT`; it is not relicensed as XMLWeave's MIT code.

The selection was fixed before engine execution: 19 complete named groups from `msMeta/Schema_w3c.xml` and `msMeta/IdentityConstraint_w3c.xml`. It includes same-namespace and chameleon includes, no-namespace and cross-namespace imports, transitive imports, invalid composition schemas, invalid identity declarations, multiple keys, derived-type value comparisons, dangling key references, namespace-sensitive references and default IDREF/IDREFS behavior. These are 19 schema expectations (six invalid) and 13 instance expectations (three invalid).

Both full upstream metadata documents are stored compressed. The manifest preserves each group's complete test list, original validity and current-status attributes, every root source and recursive local schema dependency. SHA256, Git blob identifiers and byte counts protect the original bytes. Tests compare the manifest with the full original metadata and visibly fail on every validity disagreement; no instances are filtered out.

Run `python scripts/import-w3c-structures.py PATH_TO_XSDTESTS_CHECKOUT` to reproduce the selection. The standards-conformance tests run every group against the isolated native provider and XMLWeave Java adapter with an approved in-memory schema catalogue. `node scripts/compare-java-external.mjs` separately records all raw public JAXP reference observations against those unchanged expectations, with the runtime version and any differences. OpenJDK 17 accepts `idZ012.i` (a schema-defaulted dangling IDREFS), although the upstream expected result is invalid; the native provider rejects it. This raw JDK deviation is visible in the generated report, not an altered upstream expectation. Unknown raw-JDK discrepancies fail the observation job. The XMLWeave Java adapter is separately required to match all 32 unchanged expectations, including this case. There is no network lookup during tests. This finite selection complements the NIST datatype groups; it does not establish complete W3C conformance or XSD 1.1 support.
